transcript.text: Can you describe your experience managing the daily cash book and supplier orders at your family's grocery shop?

I come from Samastipur in Bihar and studied in Hindi medium till class twelve. I am finishing BCom at a government college. On weekends I keep the daily cash book at our family grocery and place supplier orders for about 35 items. My English is still improving, so I took a six-month spoken English course. I want an MBA because small shops like ours take loans at high rates, and I want to understand how banks and suppliers work with them.
You mentioned placing supplier orders for about 35 items. What challenges did you face while managing these orders, and how did you address them?
transcript.anchor_quote: I keep the daily cash book at our family grocery and place supplier orders for about 35 items

transcript.text: I have lot of leadership qualities and I am a hardworking and dedicated person. I always give hundred percent and I am a team player, so I will do well in the MBA.

You mentioned having leadership qualities and being a dedicated team player. Can you share a specific example from your experience at your family shop or NSS volunteering where you demonstrated leadership to solve a problem or improve a process?

feedback.summary: The candidate demonstrated clear motivation for pursuing an MBA, linked directly to personal experiences in their family grocery shop and a desire to assist small shopkeepers. They showed awareness of their communication skills and took proactive steps (English course) to improve. However, the candidate struggled to provide specific examples demonstrating leadership or problem-solving during shop-related work, and did not engage fully with exploratory questions about challenges or financial knowledge. There was also limited reflection on experiences or concrete contributions, and some resistance to interview format or questioning focus.
